pass_rule: b <= 2: no conflicting commits, every honest validator commits every height; with the rule also no attacker block committed and no run worse than the same run without attack (UFLS after the strike, collapses, critical feeders); b = 2 without the rule: attacker blocks committed
known_issues: the attacker's second block is the one without the fresh state reports, the only other block the honest validators accept; with the rule it is refused whenever it leaves out a report the honest validators have held for 60 s, which here is always. A report less than 60 s old (a feeder change just before a slot) may still be left out: one slot later it is old enough

beyond f (b = 3) the rule happens to stop this attacker as well, because a block's content follows from inputs every honest validator holds; that is not a guarantee: the protocol promises nothing beyond f
C only: D runs exactly the same code; the two differ in who runs the validators, which decides how likely b compromised validators are (experiment 6), not what they can do
